title: Release lattice and capacity tiles — Qtr planning for Hosted API + Model Catalog
creator: Ayesha Patel
description:
Objective: Define a quadrant-based quarterly plan that maps release lanes (the ‘release lattice’) to capacity tiles (reserved / burst / fallback pools) for Hosted API endpoints and the Model Catalog. This ticket captures the planning artifact, stakeholder signoff checklist, and the gating criteria we will use to accept or defer model/endpoint rollouts during 2026-Q2.

Why this is different: instead of a single runway we are proposing a two-dimensional lattice (release lane vs capacity tile) to make tradeoffs explicit: high-availability lanes prioritized for enterprise SLAs use Reserved capacity tiles; experimental lanes map to Burst/Beta tiles; and a Mixed tier supports canary-to-fallback transitions. The lattice helps scheduling, cost-hedging, and automated routing policies used by Smart Routing.

Outcomes expected by the end of the cycle: a published lattice artifact (Confluence + CSV), a capacity hedge table with cost delta estimates, a canary window schedule for each lane, a set of eval gates wired into the deployment pipeline, and an ops playbook for rollback and model substitution during overload events.
acceptance_criteria: Confluence lattice doc published and reviewed by Eng/Infra/Console/Customer Success
Capacity tiles mapped to endpoint tiers with estimated per-token cost deltas and run-rate impact
Canary windows defined for each release lane (duration, sampling %, target regions)
Automated eval gate implemented in CI: hosted-fleet-evals-v2 must pass for latency and P95 token cost thresholds
Runbook added to Console Rollouts for automatic fallback to specified model variant on SLA breach
